newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ASX appoints demutualisation adviser.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ASX appoints demutualisation adviser.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Wednesday it had appointed Schroders Australia Corporate Finance to advise it in the process to demutualise and publicly list the ASX.

"ASX already possesses considerable skills including an unparalleled knowledge of market regulation and listing processes, but the board of ASX has identified the need for additional expert skills from the broader financial community," ASX chairman Maurice Newman said in a statement.
Last October, ASX members approved the demutualisation plan in a move which would clear the way for the exchange to become the first publicly listed stock exchange in the world.
Last week, Australia's Treasurer Peter Costello said the government would soon introduce legislation that would enable the ASX to demutualise.
Under the proposed legislation, individual shareholders would not be able to own more than five percent of the exchange's stock.
